title: Himachal Pradesh — Shimla, Kullu, Kasol, Spiti, Kinnaur, Kalpa, Tirthan, Kasauli
selection: Major Himachal destinations missing from earlier batches, chosen to cover the state's main circuits (Shimla hills, Kullu–Parvati, Lahaul–Spiti, Kinnaur). Light pass: overview, key facts for cards, how to reach, seasons, permits. Sources: Himachal Tourism destination pages; Wikipedia for elevations. Not found in an official source: a best season for Shimla, Kasol or Kinnaur as a whole — left out. Tirthan Valley and Kalpa added (2026-11-03) from the Great Himalayan National Park's official site, Himachal Tourism's Kullu and Kinnaur pages, HPTDC and Wikipedia. No official recommended trip length was found for either, so none is given.

KA1.claim: Kasauli is a cantonment hill station set up by the British in 1842.

evidence.quote: The cantonment was established by the British Raj in 1842 as a Colonial hill station
Elevation 2,960 m (9,710 ft)

SH6.claim: Shimla's open-air ice-skating rink runs from November to February, with a carnival around Christmas–New Year.

evidence.quote: The ice skating season lasts upto February and at around the Christmas – New Year festive week, a lively ice skating carnival is held at this open air rink.

SH3.claim: Viceregal Lodge (1888) now houses the Indian Institute of Advanced Study; parts are open to visitors.

evidence.quote: When completed in 1888, the Viceregal Lodge was one of the most flamboyant and one of first electric buildings of India.
It now houses the Indian Institute of Advanced Studies. Parts of the Lodge are open to visit for people of all ages.

KS2.claim: Kasol is popular with backpackers and is the base for treks to Malana and Kheerganga.

evidence.quote: Kasol is a popular Himalayan destination for backpackers and acts as a base for nearby treks to Malana and Kheerganga .

KU2.claim: In October the week-long Kullu Dussehra brings village deities to town on palanquins.

evidence.quote: In October, the quiet town comes to life when the week-long Kullu Dussehra festival is held.

KA5.claim: Kalka is the nearest broad-gauge station; buses run between Solan and Delhi, Chandigarh and Shimla.

evidence.quote: Nearest broad gauge railway station is at Kalka.
Luxury, deluxe and ordinary busses regularly ply between Solan – Delhi, Chandigarh and Shimla.

KU4.claim: Manikaran, on the Parvati 45 km from Kullu, has a gurdwara with a hot sulphur spring.

evidence.quote: The hot sulphur spring in the compound is therapeutic
Manikaran, 45 km from Kullu can be easily reached by private or public transport.

SP1.claim: Spiti — 'the middle land' — is a mountain cold desert of windswept valleys and quiet villages, shaped by Buddhism.

evidence.quote: A mountainous cold desert freckled with green patches over a dry weather-beaten face, fascinating valleys, windswept landscapes and quiet villages, Spiti, which loosely translates as ‘the middle land’.

SH7.claim: Light woollens do from April to October; heavy woollens are needed from November to March.

evidence.quote: Bearing a temperate climate, cotton clothes with light woolens are worn from April to October. Heavy woollends and jackets are required for the winter which starts to set in from November and lasts upto March.

KU7.claim: The park shelters Himalayan tahr, brown bear, snow leopard, blue sheep, western tragopan and monal.

evidence.quote: Home to the rare and endangered Himalayan Thar, Himalayan Brown Bear, Snow Leopard and Blue Sheep, the park is a refuge to Western Tragopan, Monal and other rare birds also.

HS22.claim: Kinnaur has good mobile signal at Reckong Peo, Kalpa and Sangla, but internet can be weak and many trek routes have none.

evidence.quote: Good mobile phone connectivity is available at Reckong Peo, Kalpa, Sangla and other destinations. However, internet connectivity may be low in most other areas. Many trek routes and offbeat destinations may not have any mobile phone connectivity at all.

KA6.claim: The Solan hills are a year-round destination: summers rarely pass 32°C and winters seldom drop below 5°C.

evidence.quote: Solan is a year around destination with mild summer temperatures that rarely rise above 32 degree Celsius and a relatively warm winter where temperature seldom drop below 5 degree Celsius.

SP5.claim: Kaza, the main town, is at about 3,650 m.

evidence.quote: Elevation 3,650 m (11,980 ft)

SP4.claim: Tabo's monastery, founded in 996 AD, is the largest monastic complex in Spiti.

evidence.quote: Founded in 996 AD, Tabo is the largest monastic complex in Spiti
Elevation 1,279 m (4,196 ft)

HS21.claim: In Spiti only BSNL mobile works well and internet is slow.

evidence.quote: Owing to its remoteness and high altitude only BSNL mobile phone network works fine in Spiti. Internet speed is slow.

HS20.claim: Kinnaur is reached on NH-22, the Hindustan–Tibet Road, with buses and taxis from Shimla and Rampur.

evidence.quote: The route is on NH – 22 (The Hindustan Tibet Road). Buses and Taxis are available at Shimla and Rampur.

KN1.claim: Kinnaur runs from Sangla's orchards to Chitkul, India's last village on the Tibet border, with Kinner Kailash seen from Kalpa and the lake at Nako.

evidence.quote: From the righteous greens of Sangla valley with well developed orchards of apricots and apples, to the magnificent panorama of Chitkul, India’s last village on Indo-Tibet border, and from the stunning sight of Mt. Kinner Kailash, abode of Lord Shiva from Kalpa, to the pristine lake at Nako village

KA4.claim: Monkey Point (Hanuman temple) is in the Air Force Station near the Lower Mall, about 4 km from the town centre.

evidence.quote: Monkey Point is situated in the Air Force Station near the Lower Mall region about 4 km (2.5 mi) from the center of town.

SH2.claim: The Ridge and the Mall remain its landmarks, with Viceregal Lodge, Christ Church, Gaiety Theatre and Gorton Castle among its colonial buildings.

evidence.quote: The Ridge and The Mall are still popular landmarks just as they were in the pre-Independence era.
The imperial Viceregal Lodge, the graceful Christ Church, Gaiety Theatre, Gorton Castle, Barnes Court and several buildings are part of the colonial architectural heritage of the town.

HS18.claim: The Kullu-Manali airport at Bhuntar is about 10 km from Kullu, with flights to Delhi and Chandigarh.

evidence.quote: The Kullu-Manali airport is at Bhuntar, about 10 km from the main town. Flights to and from Delhi and Chandigarh are available.

KU6.claim: North of Kullu, villages around Raison have riverside camping sites on the Beas.

evidence.quote: Tucked away to the north of Kullu are a cluster of small villages that offer excellent camping sites by the bank of River Beas.

HS11.claim: December to February is the coldest time in the Kullu valley, with the best chance of snow.

evidence.quote: December to February is generally the chilliest period when chances of witnessing a snowfall are more.
Elevation 1,580 m (5,180 ft)

HP9.claim: Gaggal-Kangra and Pathankot serve Kangra, Dharamshala and Chamba; Bhuntar-Kullu serves Kullu-Manali, Mandi and Lahaul-Spiti; Chandigarh and Jubbarhatti serve Shimla, Solan and Kinnaur.

evidence.quote: The Pathankot and Gaggal-Kangra airport give easy access to Kangra, Dharamshala, Chamba, Hamirpur and Una, the Bhuntar-Kullu airport to Mandi, Kullu-Manali and Lahaul-Spiti, and the Chandigarh and Jubbarhatti – Shimla airport to Shimla, Solan, Bilaspur, Mandi and Kinnaur regions.

SP3.claim: From Kaza, Key Monastery is 12 km, Kibber 18 km, Tabo 48 km, Kunzum Pass 75 km and Chandratal 98 km.

evidence.quote: Kee Monastery 12 Kibber 18
Kimic 18 Tabo 48
Kunzum Pass 75 Chandra Taal 98

SH9.claim: Chadwick Falls, near Summer Hill, are best in the July–September rains.

evidence.quote: At a walkable distance from Summer Hill are the Chadwick Falls, best visited during the rainy season that lasts from July to September.

HS31.claim: Reckong Peo holds a Tribal Festival from the last week of October into the first week of November.

evidence.quote: the Tribal Festival held every year from the last week of October into the first week of November at Reckong Peo

HS29.claim: Shimla holds its Summer Festival in early June.

evidence.quote: At the height of summer, in early June, the Shimla hold a Summer Festival

SP7.claim: The nearest airports are Bhuntar and Shimla, and the nearest broad-gauge stations Chandigarh and Kalka; the rest is by road.

evidence.quote: Flights from New Delhi and Chandigarh operate to Bhuntar and Shimla airports, which are the nearest airports to the distant cold desert.
Chandigarh and Kalka are the closest broad gauge train stations for Spiti.

SP8.claim: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Spiti near the Tibet border.

evidence.quote: Foreign tourists require Inner Line Permits to visit certain inner area of Kinnaur district and Spiti of the Lahaul-Spiti district that borders Tibet-China.

HS34.claim: Rafting on the Beas near Kullu runs March–May and September–November.

evidence.quote: In Kullu the adventure is conducted by experienced rafters, which can be experienced on long river stretches from March and May and from September to November.

HS36.claim: The Great Himalayan National Park near Kullu is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with no roads inside — only treks and camping.

evidence.quote: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and there are no roads or paved trails in this carefully conserved natural habitat.

HS13.claim: Spiti is pleasant from April to October (about 15–20°C in May–June) and can fall to −20°C in winter.

evidence.quote: Weather in Spiti is pleasant from April to October, with the May-June temperatures hovering at a comfortable 15°C and 20°C make it a good time to visit the valley.
In winters, the temperature falls to as low as minus 20 degree Celsius.

KN6.claim: In September the Fulaich fair centres on Sangla's Bering Nag temple.

evidence.quote: In September, the Fulaich fair centered around the temple does attract a large number of tourists and devotees.

SP6.claim: Ladarcha, Spiti's best-known fair, is a trade fair held in Kaza every July/August.

evidence.quote: A traditional trade fair that is held every July/August in Kaza
Ladarcha is probably the most celebrated festival of Spiti.

KU1.claim: Kullu, on the Beas, was founded as a capital in 1660 and is the gateway to Manali and the district headquarters.

evidence.quote: As a gateway to the popular destination of Manali, it is a cool escapade for tired souls.
Founded as a capital of Kullu in the year 1660, today the sprawling township serves as the administrative headquarter of the valley district.

KU5.claim: Kullu's summer (March–June) is 25–35°C; monsoon runs July–September; winter (December–February) is 5–15°C.

evidence.quote: Summer March – June 25°C – 35°C Monsoon July – September 15°C – 25°C Winter December – February 5°C – 15°C

KS1.claim: Kasol is a hamlet in the Parvati Valley between Bhuntar and Manikaran — 30 km from Bhuntar, 3.5 km from Manikaran and 36 km from Kullu.

evidence.quote: It is situated in Parvati Valley , on the banks of the Parvati River between Bhuntar and Manikaran .
It is located 30 km (19 mi) from Bhuntar , 3.5 km from Manikaran and 36 km (22 mi) from Kullu town

HS19.claim: Kullu is 40 km from Manali, 210 km from Shimla, 260 km from Chandigarh and 495 km from Delhi.

evidence.quote: Distances from Kullu (Km) Manali 40 Shimla 210 Delhi 495 Chandigarh 260

KS5.claim: Kasol has no rail or air link of its own; it is reached by road.

evidence.quote: Kasol is only connected to the rest of India by well-developed roads.

HS9.claim: Dharamshala gets very heavy rain, while Lahaul and Spiti are cold and almost rainless.

evidence.quote: The state's winter capital, Dharamsala receives very heavy rainfall, while areas like Lahaul and Spiti are cold and almost rainless.

HS16.claim: The 96.6 km narrow-gauge Kalka–Shimla railway (opened 1903, 102 tunnels) joined the Mountain Railways of India World Heritage Site in 2008.

evidence.quote: Length 96.60 km
UNESCO added the Kalka–Shimla Railway to the mountain railways of India World Heritage Site
the Kalka-Shimla railway line with 102 tunnels constructed between 1898 to 1903 has been recognised by UNESCO as World Heritage mountain railway site.

KN2.claim: It lies on the old India–Tibet trade route, cut by the Sutlej, Spiti and Baspa rivers.

evidence.quote: Lying on the ancient trade route between India and Tibet
The gushing rivers – Sutlej, Spiti, Baspa and their tributaries
Elevation 1,800 m (5,900 ft)

HS17.claim: Ordinary and luxury coaches run regularly between Delhi, Chandigarh and Shimla.

evidence.quote: Ordinary and luxury coaches regularly ply between Delhi, Chandigarh and the city.

HS15.claim: Daily flights from Delhi land at Jubbarhatti, 23 km from Shimla.

evidence.quote: There are daily flights from Delhi to Shimla Airport at Jubbarhatti, at a distance of 23 kms from the city.

KN3.claim: From Reckong Peo, Kalpa is 13 km, Sangla 38 km, Chitkul 65 km, Nako 102 km and Shimla 230 km.

evidence.quote: Kalpa 13 Nako 102 Sangla 38 Chitkul 65 Shimla 230

SH4.claim: Jakhoo Temple sits on Shimla's highest hill at 2,445 m, a half-hour climb from the Ridge or by ropeway.

evidence.quote: Overlooking the hill station at 2,445 meters altitude, Jakhoo Hill is Shimla city’s acme and home to Lord Hanuman.
The daunting half-an-hour uphill climb from The Ridge finally ends at Jakhoo Temple. Ropeway service to Jakhoo temple is also available.

KS3.claim: A bridge divides Kasol into old and new townships, with a growing number of guesthouses, camps and hotels; buses and taxis are easy to find.

evidence.quote: Once a quaint village that is now divided by a bridge into old and new townships has only recently expanded to have growing number of guesthouses, camps and hotels
Buses regularly ply to Kasol and taxis are also easily available for hire.

SP2.claim: Spiti lies at well over 3,000 m, with hamlets, trekking trails, ancient monasteries and lakes.

evidence.quote: Located at well over 3,000 m altitude high up in the mountains, Spiti welcomes travellers to its postcard-perfect hamlets, surreal landscapes, plentiful trekking trails, ancient monasteries and scenic lakes.

SH1.claim: Shimla, Himachal's capital, was the British summer capital and keeps its colonial buildings.

evidence.quote: the state capital of Himachal Pradesh is one of the most popular hill stations of India.
they elevated the small township into the summer capital of an empire sprawling the sub-continent.

HS32.claim: Lossar, Spiti's New Year, usually falls in February, with masked chham dances at the monasteries.

evidence.quote: is usually celebrated in February to mark the advent of the New Year.
The prime attraction of the festival at the monasteries is a ritual chham dance by lamas adorning elaborate costumes and masks.
Elevation 2,376 m (7,795 ft)

HS14.claim: Regular buses run Manali–Kaza from July to October and Shimla–Kinnaur–Kaza from May to October; sturdy off-road taxis are recommended.

evidence.quote: From Manali to Kaza, there are regular buses from July to October and from Shimla via Kinnaur, there are regular buses from May to October.
Sturdy vehicles used as off-roading taxis are recommended for a travel tour to Spiti from Manali or Shimla.

KN7.claim: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Kinnaur near the Tibet border.

evidence.quote: Foreign tourists require Inner Line Permits to visit certain inner area of Kinnaur district and Spiti of the Lahaul-Spiti district that borders Tibet-China.

KN4.claim: The nearest railhead and airport are both at Shimla, 244 km and 267 km away.

evidence.quote: Nearest Railhead (244 Km) is Shimla .
Nearest Airport (267 Km) is Shimla .

KA2.claim: Kasauli is about 25–27 km from Solan, 58 km from Chandigarh and 77 km from Shimla.

evidence.quote: 25 km (16 mi) from Solan , 77 km (48 mi) from Shimla , 58 km (36 mi) from Chandigarh
Kasauli 27

HP14.claim: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Kinnaur and Spiti on the Tibet border; permits are issued in New Delhi (Himachal Bhawan), Shimla, Reckong Peo and at SDM offices in Kalpa, Kaza and Manali.

evidence.quote: Foreign tourists require Inner Line Permits to visit certain inner area of Kinnaur district and Spiti of the Lahaul-Spiti district that borders Tibet-China.

The Permits are issued by Resident Commissioner of Himachal Pradesh, Himachal Bhawan, 27, Sikandra Road, New Delhi and at Deputy Commissioner’s office at Shimla, Kinnaur at Reckong Peo and SDM office at Kalpa, Kaza, Manali.

HP25.claim: Stay in hotels, guest houses and homestays registered with the Department of Tourism.

evidence.quote: Stay only in hotel/guest houses/home stays that are registered with the Department of Tourism.

TV1.claim: Tirthan Valley lies in the eco-zone of the Great Himalayan National Park, about 70 km from Kullu, and is known for its river, pine forests and birdlife.

evidence.quote: nestled in the eco-rich buffer zone of the Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP)
Located about 70 km from Kullu
Known for its pristine river, lush pine forests, snow-capped peaks, and vibrant biodiversity

TV2.claim: The Tirthan rises at a spring below Hanskund Peak (4,800 m), meets the Palchan stream at Gushaini and joins the Beas at Larji.

evidence.quote: originates at Hanskund Peak (4800m)
it joins Palchan Nallah at Gushaini
continues till Larji, where Tirthan and Sainj streams merge with the Beas River

TV3.claim: The valley covers 754 sq km, forming the Tirthan Wildlife Sanctuary and part of the national park.

evidence.quote: The valley covers an area of 754 Sq. Kms and the same constitutes Tirthan Wildlife Sanctuary and part of GHNP.

TV4.claim: The snow-fed Tirthan holds plenty of trout; fishing is allowed in designated eco-zone stretches and is best from April to October.

evidence.quote: The clear waters of the snow fed River Tirthan hold a lot of trout fish.
an activity permitted in designated eco-zones, is best undertaken from April through October

TV5.claim: Aut, on the Chandigarh–Manali highway, is the turn-off; Gushaini, the trekking roadhead, is about 52 km from Aut on an all-weather road, and buses and taxis run from Kullu, Manali and Mandi.

evidence.quote: The roadhead for trekking in Tirthan Valley is at Gushaini, around 52km from Aut on an all-weather road.
serves as the main access point for further travel by taxi or bus to villages like Gushaini
Regular buses and taxis operate from Kullu

TV6.claim: The nearest airport is Bhuntar, about 50 km from the park, with regular flights from Delhi; the nearest station is Joginder Nagar on the narrow-gauge line, and the nearest major station is Chandigarh, 296 km away.

evidence.quote: about 50 km away, with regular flights from Delhi
The nearest railway station is Joginder Nagar
The closest major railway station to GHNP is 296km away, in Chandigarh

TV7.claim: Trekking in the park's core zone is best from April to June and from September to November.

evidence.quote: is best enjoyed from April to June and again from September to November

TV8.claim: Birding is good all year but best from March to June and September to November; for the western tragopan, March–May and October–November.

evidence.quote: the months from March to June and September to November offer the highest chances of spotting a wide variety of Himalayan bird species
is particularly recommended from March to May and October to November

TV9.claim: Entry to the park is by permit, with extra charges for cameras; core-zone permits are issued at the Shamshi head office and the range office at Shairopa in Tirthan Valley. Check current fees with the park.

evidence.quote: Entrance to the park is by permit, with additional charges for still and video cameras.
Permits for the core zone can be obtained at the head office in Shamshi and the range offices in Shairopa (Tirthan Valley)
Please check with the park authorities for latest fees.

TV10.claim: Trekking routes must be approved by a park range officer, multi-day trekkers must hire certified guides and porters, and all activities inside the park are on foot.

evidence.quote: Trekking routes must be discussed with and approved by a GHNP range officer before entering the park.
Multi-day trekkers must engage certified guides and porters.
there is no provision for motor safaris

TV11.claim: Visitors staying more than a day in the park are strongly advised to buy travel insurance that covers emergency treatment and evacuation.

evidence.quote: Visitors of more than one day to GHNP are strongly advised to buy travel insurance that covers emergency medical treatment and evacuation.

TV12.claim: The rains fall mainly from mid-June to mid-September; spring (April–June) is one of the best times to visit; winter snow ranges from a few centimetres in the lower valleys to over two metres up high, and the riverside villages get little snow.

evidence.quote: especially between mid-June and mid-September
Spring is one of the best times to visit
Snowfall ranges from a few centimetres in the lower valleys to over two meters in alpine regions.
receive little snowfall once or twice each winter

TV13.claim: Banjar is the valley's main market; nearby are Jibhi, Shoja, Jalori Pass, Chehni Kothi (the fort of the deity Shringa Rishi) and the Shairopa forest complex.

evidence.quote: Banjar town being the main marketplace in Tirthan Valley
Chehni fort of deity Shringa Rishi
Jibhi town, Shoja, Jalori Pass

TV14.claim: Shoja is the base for easy treks to Jalori Pass, Serolsar Lake, Takrasi and Khanag; Jalori Pass divides the Sutlej and Beas catchments.

evidence.quote: Shoja is also the base for easy treks to Jalori Pass, Serolsar Lake, Takrasi and Khanag.
Jalori demarcates the catchments of River Satluj from Beas.

TV15.claim: Gushaini, where the Tirthan and Palchan meet, is a sacred site for pilgrims and locals.

evidence.quote: a picturesque village where the Tirthan and Palchan rivers meet
making it a revered site for pilgrims and locals alike

TV16.claim: Expect limited connectivity and remote villages; carry essentials and travel with a local guide.

evidence.quote: be prepared for limited connectivity, remote villages, and high-altitude terrain
It’s recommended to carry essentials, travel with a local guide, and check the weather conditions ahead.

TV17.claim: Rock climbing, river crossing and abseiling run in the ecozone from March to June and September to November; camping and sightseeing are best from March to November.

evidence.quote: Adventure seekers can indulge in rock climbing, river crossing, and abseiling in the ecozone from March to June and again from September to November.
with optimal conditions between March and November

TV18.claim: There is also a route from Shimla over Jalori Pass, past Shoja and cedar forests.

evidence.quote: where one can travel through the Jalori pass, seeing villages like Shoja and cedar forests along the way to the valley

TV19.claim: Larji, where the Sainj, Tirthan and Beas meet on the Aut–Luhari road, is the gateway to the Sainj and Tirthan valleys.

evidence.quote: Larji is situated along the Aut–Luhari road
serves as the gateway to the Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP) and its two major valleys

TV20.claim: Keep noise to a minimum, carry out non-biodegradable litter, and ask before photographing ecozone residents.

evidence.quote: Noise whilst trekking in the forest and whilst observing wildlife must be kept to an absolute minimum.
Non-biodegradable litter must be kept with you and disposed of away from GHNP and the ecozone.
Permission must be obtained before photographing residents of the ecozone or entering their property.

KP1.claim: Kalpa sits 13 km above Reckong Peo, at about 2,960 m.

evidence.quote: Going past Reckong Peo as you ascend higher (13 km) into the hillside, you reach Kalpa
It has an average elevation of 2,960 metres (9,711 feet)

KP2.claim: Kalpa faces the Kinner Kailash range; the sacred Shivling rock on Kailash can be seen from here.

evidence.quote: It sits at the base of the snow-capped Kinnaur Kailash ranges.
Also visible from here is the sacred Shivling rock on the Kailash mountain

KP3.claim: The Narayan-Nagini temple, with dragons carved round its porch pillars, stands a stone's throw from the Hu-Bu-Lan-Kar gompa, said to be founded by Rinchen Zangpo (950–1055 AD).

evidence.quote: The finely decorated Narayan-Nagini temple is exemplary about the local craftsmanship
The temple features amazingly carved dragons coiled around porch pillars
A Buddhist temple said to be founded by missionary Rinchen Zangpo (950-1055 AD)
The Hu-Bu-Lan-Kar gompa is in close proximity of Kalpa.

KP4.claim: Kalpa was a tehsil headquarters in colonial times and later Kinnaur's district headquarters, before that moved to Reckong Peo.

evidence.quote: It was tehsil headquarter during colonial times and later became district headquarter of Kinnaur before it was shifted to Reckong Peo.

KP5.claim: Kalpa is surrounded by deodar, apple orchards and chilgoza (pine-nut) trees.

evidence.quote: Kalpa is surrounded by Deodar, apple, and pinus gerardiana chilghoza trees.

KP6.claim: Kothi, between Reckong Peo and Kalpa, is an orchard village whose temple to Chandika Devi looks out on Kinner Kailash.

evidence.quote: Kothi, also referred to as Koshtampi, is a large village between Reckong Peo, the district headquarter and Kalpa
Kothi has a temple dedicated to the goddess Chandika Devi.

KP7.claim: Winters are long (October–May) with 1.5–2 m of snow and lows near −20°C; summers (June–September) are short, and warm clothing may be needed even then.

evidence.quote: with long winters from October to May, and short summers from June to September
the temperature can drop to as low as −20 °C
Warm clothing may be necessary even in the summer.

KP8.claim: April to October is a good time to visit Kinnaur; from November temperatures fall, dropping well below freezing in December and January.

evidence.quote: April to October is a good time to visit Kinnaur.
they do drop well below the freezing point in December and January

KP9.claim: HPTDC's Kinner Kailash hotel in Kalpa is closed December–March; Shimla to Kalpa is 222 km (about eight hours) and Chandigarh to Kalpa 338 km (about 11 hours).

evidence.quote: Closed from December - March due to extreme weather conditions
Shimla to Kalpa- 222 KM – Eight hours drive
Chandigarh to Kalpa: 338 KM – 11 hours drive

KP10.claim: Kalpa holds the liveliest Fulaich, the mid-September flower festival that marks the end of summer.

evidence.quote: While Kalpa holds a most vibrant function
Fulaich fair is held in mid-September.

KP11.claim: For a serious emergency you need the regional hospital at Reckong Peo, Rampur Bushahr or Shimla.

evidence.quote: To meet any serious emergency, one has to get to the regional hospital at Reckong Peo, Rampur Bushair or Shimla

KP12.claim: Kalpa can also be reached from Manali over Kunzum Pass via Kaza, about 400 km.

evidence.quote: One can also reach Kalpa via Manali – Rohtang Pass – Kunzam Pass – Kaza (400 Km).

KP13.claim: Lippa, with three Buddhist monasteries, is easily reached from Kalpa or Reckong Peo.

evidence.quote: Lippa is a small village that can be easily reached from Kalpa or Reckong Peo.

KP14.claim: Kinnaur is chilly all year: light woollens in summer with heavy woollens for the evenings, and heavy woollens in winter.

evidence.quote: In summers light woollens would be sufficient to live the days but heavy woollens and jackets need to carried along

places.seoDescription: Plan Shimla: the Ridge and Mall, Viceregal Lodge, Jakhoo Temple, the Kalka–Shimla toy train, winter ice skating and how to get there.

images.alt: Christ Church's yellow facade on the Ridge in Shimla
images.caption: Christ Church on the Ridge, Shimla

items.title: Altitude
items.body: About 2,376 m

items.title: Known for
items.body: The Ridge, Mall Road and the toy train

items.title: Nearest airport
items.body: Jubbarhatti, 23 km

items.title: Ice skating
items.body: November–February

overview.text:
Shimla, the capital of Himachal Pradesh, grew from a small township into the summer capital of British India, and its colonial core still shows it. The Ridge and the Mall remain the town's landmarks, lined by Christ Church, the Gaiety Theatre and Gorton Castle, and the Viceregal Lodge of 1888 now houses the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, with parts open to visitors.

Above the town, Jakhoo Temple stands on Shimla's highest hill at 2,445 m — a half-hour climb from the Ridge, or a ropeway ride. The 96 km Kalka–Shimla railway, opened in 1903 with 102 tunnels, is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is the slow, scenic way up. Shimla also makes a base for the drive into Kinnaur along the Hindustan–Tibet Road.

items.body: Walk the Ridge and the Mall, past Christ Church, the Gaiety Theatre and Scandal Point.
Visit the Viceregal Lodge (1888), now the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.
Climb or take the ropeway to Jakhoo Temple at 2,445 m.
Ride the Kalka–Shimla toy train.
Skate on the open-air ice rink between November and February.
See Chadwick Falls near Summer Hill in the July–September rains.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: daily flights from Delhi land at Jubbarhatti, 23 km from Shimla; Chandigarh is the other option.

By rail: take a broad-gauge train to Kalka, then the narrow-gauge Kalka–Shimla line.

By road: ordinary and luxury coaches run regularly from Delhi and Chandigarh.

best_time.text: Light woollens do from April to October; winter sets in from November and lasts until March, when heavy woollens and jackets are needed. The Summer Festival is held in early June, and the ice-skating season runs until February, with a carnival around Christmas and New Year.

places.name: Kullu
places.summary: The Beas valley's old capital and district town: gateway to Manali, home of the October Dussehra, with rafting, riverside camping and the Great Himalayan National Park nearby.
places.seoTitle: Kullu Travel Guide: Dussehra, Rafting & Valley
places.seoDescription: Plan Kullu: the October Dussehra, rafting on the Beas, camping at Raison, Manikaran's hot spring, the Great Himalayan National Park and getting there.

overview.text:
Kullu spreads along the Beas river. Founded as a capital in 1660, it is now the district headquarters and the gateway to Manali, 40 km up the valley.

In October the week-long Kullu Dussehra fills the town as village deities arrive on palanquins. The rest of the year the valley is for the outdoors: rafting on long stretches of the Beas, riverside camping around Raison, and the Great Himalayan National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with no roads inside, home to Himalayan tahr, brown bear, snow leopard and the western tragopan. Manikaran's gurdwara and hot sulphur spring are 45 km away on the Parvati.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: the Kullu–Manali airport at Bhuntar is about 10 km away, with flights to Delhi and Chandigarh.

By road: Kullu is 260 km from Chandigarh and 495 km from Delhi; luxury and ordinary coaches run from Delhi, Chandigarh, Shimla and Dharamshala.

best_time.text: Summer (March–June) is 25–35°C in the valley, the monsoon runs from July to September, and winter (December–February) is 5–15°C with the best chance of snow. Come in October for Dussehra; rafting runs March–May and September–November.

overview.text:
Kasol sits on the banks of the Parvati river between Bhuntar and Manikaran, 36 km from Kullu town. Once a quiet village, it is now split by a bridge into an old and a new township, with a growing number of guesthouses, camps and hotels.

It is a popular stop for backpackers and the usual base for treks to Malana and Kheerganga. The Manikaran gurdwara, with its hot sulphur spring, is just 3.5 km up the valley. There is no railway or airport here — Kasol is reached by road, with regular buses and easy-to-find taxis.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Bhuntar (Kullu–Manali airport) is about 30 km away.

By road: buses run regularly to Kasol and taxis are easy to hire; there is no rail link.

places.name: Spiti Valley
places.summary: Himachal's high cold desert on the Tibet border: thousand-year-old monasteries, villages above 3,000 m and roads open only part of the year.
places.seoTitle: Spiti Valley Travel Guide: Kaza, Key & Tabo
places.seoDescription: Plan Spiti Valley: Kaza, Key and Tabo monasteries, Kunzum Pass and Chandratal, the April–October season, buses from Manali and Shimla and permits.

images.alt: Key Monastery's white buildings stacked on a dry hill in Spiti
images.caption: Key Monastery, Spiti

items.title: Altitude
items.body: Kaza about 3,650 m

items.title: Best time
items.body: April–October

items.title: Buses
items.body: Manali–Kaza Jul–Oct · via Kinnaur May–Oct

items.title: Mobile
items.body: Only BSNL works well

overview.text:
Spiti — 'the middle land' — is a mountain cold desert of windswept valleys and quiet villages on the Tibet border, lying at well over 3,000 m. Buddhism shapes daily life, and its monasteries are the main draw: Key is 12 km from Kaza, and Tabo's, founded in 996 AD, is the largest monastic complex in the valley.

From Kaza, the main town at about 3,650 m, roads lead to Kibber (18 km), Tabo (48 km), Kunzum Pass (75 km) and Chandratal (98 km). The valley sits in the rain shadow and is pleasant from April to October; in winter it can fall to −20°C. Plan for limited signal — only BSNL works well — and note that foreigners need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas.

how_to_reach.text:
By road from Manali: regular buses to Kaza run from July to October.

By road from Shimla: buses via Kinnaur run from May to October; sturdy off-road taxis are recommended on both routes.

By air and rail: the nearest airports are Bhuntar and Shimla, and the nearest broad-gauge stations Chandigarh and Kalka — the rest is by road.

best_time.text: Spiti is pleasant from April to October, around 15–20°C in May and June, and stays almost rainless during the monsoon. Winter drops to −20°C. Ladarcha, the big trade fair at Kaza, is held in July/August; Lossar, the New Year, usually falls in February.

items.title: Permits
items.body: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas near the Tibet border.

items.title: Mobile and internet
items.body: Only BSNL mobile works well; internet is slow.

places.name: Kinnaur
places.summary: The Sutlej valley on the old India–Tibet trade route: Sangla's orchards, Chitkul on the border, Kalpa facing Kinner Kailash and Nako's lake.
places.seoTitle: Kinnaur Travel Guide: Kalpa, Sangla & Chitkul
places.seoDescription: Plan Kinnaur: Kalpa and Kinner Kailash, Sangla and Chitkul, Nako, distances from Reckong Peo, the Hindustan–Tibet Road, festivals and permits.

items.title: Known for
items.body: Kalpa, Sangla, Chitkul and Nako

overview.text:
Kinnaur lies on the ancient trade route between India and Tibet, its valleys cut by the Sutlej, Spiti and Baspa rivers. It runs from the apple and apricot orchards of the Sangla valley to Chitkul, India's last village on the Tibet border, and from Kalpa — at about 2,960 m, facing Kinner Kailash — to the lake at Nako.

Reckong Peo is the district town: Kalpa is 13 km away, Sangla 38 km, Chitkul 65 km and Nako 102 km. The road in is NH-22, the Hindustan–Tibet Road, and the September Fulaich fair at Sangla and the Tribal Festival at Reckong Peo in late October are the times to see local culture.

how_to_reach.text:
By road: Kinnaur is on NH-22, the Hindustan–Tibet Road; buses and taxis leave from Shimla and Rampur. Reckong Peo is 230 km from Shimla.

By rail and air: the nearest railhead and airport are both at Shimla, 244 km and 267 km away.

items.title: Permits
items.body: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas near the Tibet border.

items.title: Mobile and internet
items.body: Good mobile signal at Reckong Peo, Kalpa and Sangla, but internet can be weak and many trek routes have none.

overview.text:
Kasauli is a small cantonment town in Solan district, set up by the British in 1842 as a hill station, and it keeps much of that unhurried feel. It is about 25–27 km from Solan, 58 km from Chandigarh and 77 km from Shimla, which makes it one of the easiest hill escapes from the plains.

Monkey Point, the Hanuman temple in the Air Force Station near the Lower Mall, is about 4 km from the town centre. The Solan hills are mild all year — summers rarely pass 32°C and winters seldom drop below 5°C.

how_to_reach.text:
By rail: Kalka is the nearest broad-gauge station.

By road: Chandigarh is about 58 km away; buses run between Solan and Delhi, Chandigarh and Shimla.

places.name: Tirthan Valley
places.summary: A quiet river valley in the eco-zone of the Great Himalayan National Park: trout streams, cedar forest, village homestays and the park's trekking roadhead at Gushaini.
places.seoTitle: Tirthan Valley Travel Guide: GHNP, Trout & Treks
places.seoDescription: Plan Tirthan Valley: the Great Himalayan National Park, trekking seasons and permits, trout fishing, Jibhi, Shoja and Jalori Pass, and how to get there from Aut.

images.alt: The Tirthan river rushing over boulders between steep green hillsides
images.caption: The Tirthan river, Tirthan Valley

images.alt: Clear green water of the Tirthan pouring past rocks and forest
images.caption: The Tirthan river

items.title: Where
items.body: Kullu district, about 70 km from Kullu

items.title: Known for
items.body: Great Himalayan National Park, trout and birding

items.title: Trekking
items.body: April–June, September–November

items.title: Trout fishing
items.body: April–October, designated stretches

items.title: Roadhead
items.body: Gushaini, 52 km from Aut

overview.text:
Tirthan Valley lies in the eco-zone of the Great Himalayan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, about 70 km from Kullu. The Tirthan rises below Hanskund Peak (4,800 m), meets the Palchan stream at Gushaini and joins the Beas at Larji; its 754 sq km form the Tirthan Wildlife Sanctuary and part of the park.

People come for slow days by a trout river, birding and forest walks, and for the park's treks, which start at Gushaini. Banjar is the valley's market town, and Jibhi, Shoja, Jalori Pass and Chehni Kothi are close by. Inside the park there are no roads — everything is on foot, by permit.

items.body: Trek into the Great Himalayan National Park from Gushaini (April–June, September–November) with a permit and certified guides.
Fish for trout in the designated eco-zone stretches of the Tirthan (April–October).
Go birding — best March–June and September–November; for the western tragopan, March–May and October–November.
Walk from Shoja to Jalori Pass or Serolsar Lake — easy treks.
Visit Chehni Kothi, the fort of the deity Shringa Rishi, and the Shairopa forest complex.
Try rock climbing, river crossing and abseiling in the ecozone (March–June, September–November).
Stop at Gushaini, where the Tirthan and Palchan meet — a sacred spot for pilgrims and locals.

how_to_reach.text:
By road: turn off the Chandigarh–Manali highway at Aut, near Larji. Gushaini, the trekking roadhead, is about 52 km from Aut on an all-weather road, and buses and taxis run from Kullu, Manali and Mandi. From Shimla there is also a route over Jalori Pass, past Shoja.

By air: Bhuntar is the nearest airport, about 50 km from the park, with regular flights from Delhi.

By rail: the nearest station is Joginder Nagar, on the narrow-gauge line; the nearest major station is Chandigarh, 296 km away.

best_time.text: Spring (April–June) is one of the best times, and trekking is best from April to June and September to November. The rains fall mainly from mid-June to mid-September. In winter the riverside villages get only a little snow, while the high country gets well over a metre.

items.title: Park permits
items.body: Entry is by permit, with extra camera charges. Core-zone permits come from the Shamshi head office or the Shairopa range office in Tirthan. Check current fees with the park.

items.title: Trekking rules
items.body: Routes must be approved by a range officer; multi-day trekkers must hire certified guides and porters.

items.title: Insurance
items.body: For more than a day in the park, buy travel insurance that covers emergency treatment and evacuation.

items.title: Signal
items.body: Expect limited connectivity; carry essentials and travel with a local guide.

items.title: Respect the park
items.body: Keep noise down, carry out non-biodegradable litter, and ask before photographing residents.

items.title: Is Tirthan Valley part of the Great Himalayan National Park?
items.body: It is in the park's eco-zone, and its 754 sq km form the Tirthan Wildlife Sanctuary and part of the park. Gushaini is the trekking roadhead.

items.title: How do I get to Tirthan Valley?
items.body: Turn off the Chandigarh–Manali highway at Aut; Gushaini is about 52 km on. Buses and taxis run from Kullu, Manali and Mandi. Bhuntar airport is about 50 km from the park.

items.title: Do I need a permit?
items.body: Yes, to enter the national park. Core-zone permits are issued at Shamshi and at the Shairopa range office; multi-day trekkers must hire certified guides.

items.title: When can I fish for trout?
items.body: April to October, in the designated eco-zone stretches.

items.title: When should I go?
items.body: April to June and September to November for trekking and birding. Avoid mid-June to mid-September, the rainy season.

places.name: Kalpa
places.summary: An orchard village 13 km above Reckong Peo, facing the Kinner Kailash range — carved temples, a thousand-year-old gompa and HPTDC's hotel at about 2,960 m.
places.seoTitle: Kalpa Travel Guide: Kinner Kailash Views, Kinnaur
places.seoDescription: Plan Kalpa in Kinnaur: Kinner Kailash and the Shivling, the Narayan-Nagini temple and Hu-Bu-Lan-Kar gompa, Kothi, season, drive times and permits.

images.alt: Kalpa's houses below the snow-covered Kinner Kailash range, with bare orchard trees in front
images.caption: Kalpa and the Kinner Kailash range

images.alt: Snow peaks of the Kinnaur Kailash range seen from Kalpa
images.caption: Kinnaur Kailash from Kalpa

items.title: Altitude
items.body: About 2,960 m

items.title: Known for
items.body: Views of Kinner Kailash

items.title: From Reckong Peo
items.body: 13 km

items.title: From Shimla
items.body: 222 km, about 8 hours

items.title: Best time
items.body: April–October

overview.text:
Kalpa sits 13 km above Reckong Peo at about 2,960 m, facing the Kinner Kailash range — on a clear day you can see the sacred Shivling rock on Kailash. It was a colonial tehsil headquarters and later Kinnaur's district headquarters before that moved to Reckong Peo, and it is still ringed by deodar, apple orchards and chilgoza pines.

Its Narayan-Nagini temple, with dragons carved round the porch pillars, stands a stone's throw from the Hu-Bu-Lan-Kar gompa, said to have been founded by Rinchen Zangpo. Kalpa holds the liveliest Fulaich flower festival in mid-September, and it makes a natural first night on the road from Shimla into Kinnaur and Spiti.

items.body: Watch the light change on Kinner Kailash and the Shivling rock.
See the carved Narayan-Nagini temple and the Hu-Bu-Lan-Kar gompa next to it.
Walk down to Kothi, an orchard village with a temple to Chandika Devi.
Come in mid-September for Fulaich, the flower festival.
Day-trip to Sangla (38 km from Reckong Peo) and Chitkul (65 km), India's last village on the Tibet border.
Visit Lippa, with three Buddhist monasteries, easily reached from Kalpa.

how_to_reach.text:
By road from Shimla: 222 km on NH-22, the Hindustan–Tibet Road — about eight hours by HPTDC's count. Buses and taxis run from Shimla and Rampur to Reckong Peo, 13 km below Kalpa. Chandigarh is 338 km, about 11 hours.

From Spiti: Kalpa can also be reached from Manali over Kunzum Pass via Kaza, about 400 km, in the open season.

By air and rail: the nearest airport and railhead are both at Shimla.

best_time.text: April to October is the season. Winters are long — October to May — with 1.5–2 m of snow and lows near −20°C, and HPTDC's hotel closes December to March. Even in summer evenings are cold, so carry warm layers.

items.title: Permits
items.body: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Kinnaur; Reckong Peo, just below Kalpa, is one of the places that issue it.

items.title: Mobile signal
items.body: Good at Reckong Peo, Kalpa and Sangla, but internet can be weak and many trek routes have none.

items.title: Health
items.body: For a serious emergency you need the regional hospital at Reckong Peo, Rampur Bushahr or Shimla.

items.title: Where to stay
items.body: HPTDC runs The Kinner Kailash (closed December–March); choose other stays registered with the Department of Tourism.

items.title: Clothing
items.body: Light woollens by day in summer, heavy woollens and a jacket for evenings; heavy woollens in winter.

items.title: How far is Kalpa from Shimla?
items.body: 222 km on the Hindustan–Tibet Road, about eight hours by HPTDC's count.

items.title: What is Kalpa famous for?
items.body: Its view of the Kinner Kailash range and the Shivling rock, its carved Narayan-Nagini temple and the Hu-Bu-Lan-Kar gompa.

items.title: When is the best time to visit Kalpa?
items.body: April to October. Winters run October to May with heavy snow, and HPTDC's hotel closes December to March.

items.title: Do I need a permit for Kalpa?
items.body: Foreign tourists need an Inner Line Permit for some inner areas of Kinnaur beyond Kalpa; it can be obtained at Reckong Peo, 13 km below.

items.title: Is Kalpa a good stop on the way to Spiti?
items.body: Yes — it is the usual first night on the Shimla side, at about 2,960 m.
